claim: For every integer \(p\ge1\) and residue \(r\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\), let \(L_{p,r}=\{a^n:n\ge0,\ n\equiv r\pmod p\}\). The minimum number of states of a loop-free, epsilon-free NFA for \(L_{p,r}\) whose transitions all cross a fixed bipartition and whose underlying simple transition graph is a cactus equals \(\operatorname{lcm}(p,2)\); among unrestricted epsilon-free NFAs, which may have self-loops, the minimum is \(p\). Thus the structural constraint doubles the exact state minimum when \(p\) is odd and adds no states when \(p\) is even.
integrity_notes: The proof is an analytic lower bound and matching explicit construction; no finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.
Originality is assessed against the inspected literature and published-finding corpus searches, not as a guarantee that no related statement exists.
scientific_limitations: The exact formula is proved only for single-residue unary languages \(L_{p,r}\); it is not a state-complexity formula for arbitrary unary regular languages or multi-letter languages.
No bound is claimed for the full regular-expression-to-bipartite-cactus construction.
title: Sharp state cost of unary residue languages in bipartite-cactus automata
